tasks.short: Build prototype optomechanical devices for cameras sights or telescopes

steps.what: Read the prototype drawing for optomechanical devices
Build prototype equipment such as aerial cameras gun sights or telescopes
Judge image and fit of the built devices against the drawing

tasks.design: The technician reads the prototype drawing in {DOCS}, then builds the optomechanical device on the bench, including aerial cameras, gun sights, or telescopes. The image and the mechanical fit stay a bench judgement. No second record is written, and no draft replaces the build.
tasks.previous_blocker: Image quality and mechanical fit depend on the optic in hand, not on a file.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster coding does not align a lens or judge a live image.
tasks.still_hard: The technician still assembles the optic and judges the image against the drawing.
tasks.human_edge: Scatter, tilt and strain show up on the bench in ways the drawing does not record.
tasks.altitude: The week is unchanged. The technician still builds the prototype and still makes the image call.

reach.task: Set the optical tolerance the prototype must meet
reach.learn: Which image defect is a build error and which is a tolerance the engineer owns

evidence.claim: Aligning lenses and judging a live image are situational bench work. The group's published tools cover drafting paperwork, not this physical build, and no measured drafting result applies.

assumptions: The task is the build, not a log entry. No paperwork baseline is added.
There is no field map to maintain. Focal upkeep is zero because nothing is configured.
unknowns: Whether this shop keeps a written build log besides the drawing.
research_questions: How often a prototype fails the image check for a reason the drawing did not state?

already_counted.description: Reading the drawing, building the device, and judging image and fit stay bench time.

incremental.description: No map or template to keep. A drawing change is a new job, not weekly upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The build, the alignment and the image check stay on the bench. None of those steps is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose processing steps with microscopy profilometry or ellipsometry

steps.what: Perform diagnostic analyses of processing steps using microscopy
Read stored traces from profilometry and ellipsometry devices
Judge the analytical metrological tools result and state accepted numbers
Copy the accepted readings into the second process log

tasks.design: The technician runs the metrology tool and reads the stored trace in the instrument file {OTHER}, then states the accepted numbers and the spec call. A separate gated copy writes only those fields into the process log {OPS_SYSTEM}, a second record. If the instrument file is the only record, the copy does not run.
tasks.previous_blocker: The instrument file and the process log are separate, and the pass call is not a column the instrument writes.
tasks.enabler_now: A fixed field copy can move numbers the technician has already accepted. Native export is tried first; the cut is only that retype.
tasks.still_hard: The technician still mounts the part, reads the trace, and decides whether the process step is in spec.
tasks.human_edge: The technician names the process fault. The copy does not.
tasks.altitude: The technician still runs the measurement and still makes the spec call. The retype of accepted numbers into the process log is the only change.

reach.task: Confirm the instrument is in calibration before a process reading is trusted
reach.learn: Which readings are void when the calibration date has lapsed

evidence.claim: DewesoftX records test data and produces PDF or Word reports of that stored data. That is a record of stored channels, not a named process fault, and it is not this task's time cut.
Deciding whether a process step is in spec stays with the technician. The only change is copying numbers already accepted from the instrument file into a separate process log.

assumptions: Today the photonics technician retypes a few accepted readings from the instrument file {OTHER} into a separate process traveler {OPS_SYSTEM}. If the instrument file is the only record, s4 does not run.
s3 produces the fields the copy may use: accepted_thickness, accepted_roughness, spec_call, and recipe_step. The technician states them. A later edit voids the file.
Column names are fixed at build. The technician does not maintain the map. A renamed column or a new instrument is a new build, so focal upkeep is zero.
Today's actor on the retype is the photonics technician. The machine is only the future fate of that copy.
Access is to the instrument export and the process log. No personal data is copied. Staff consultation follows national rules only if the shop treats the log change as a change in assigned work.
unknowns: Whether accepted numbers are retyped into a process traveler, or left only in the instrument file.
research_questions: What share of process steps have a traveler that is a different record from the instrument file?

already_counted.description: Running the tool, reading the trace, and stating the accepted numbers stay the technician's time.

incremental.description: No weekly map upkeep. A new instrument or a renamed log column is a new build.

approvals.approved_version: The accepted readings as the technician stated them at s3, limited to accepted_thickness, accepted_roughness, spec_call and recipe_step. A later edit voids the file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the instrument file is the only record, the copy into a process log does not run. If the technician already retypes a few accepted numbers into a separate traveler, part of that retype returns. The mount, the trace reading and the spec call stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design build or modify fixtures that assemble parts

steps.what: Read the drawing of the parts the fixture must hold
Design or modify fixtures and mark datum clamp and clearance
Build the fixture so it can assemble parts
Seat one part and judge whether the fixture clamps without strain

tasks.design: The technician reads the part drawing in {DOCS}, designs or modifies the fixture on that drawing, then builds it and seats a part. The fit judgement stays on the bench. No generated sketch is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Datum, clamp and clearance are judged on the real part.
tasks.enabler_now: A drawing aid would still leave the build and the seat to the technician.
tasks.still_hard: The technician still designs the fixture and proves it on a part.
tasks.human_edge: Strain and slip show up when a part is seated, which a sketch does not show.
tasks.altitude: The week is unchanged. The technician still designs, builds and proves the fixture.

reach.task: Specify the datum the fixture must hold
reach.learn: Which clamp force marks the optic and which force is safe

evidence.claim: Fixture fit on a real part is situational. No measured drafting result in this group applies to seating a part in a fixture.

assumptions: The technician designs the fixture by hand and builds it. No machine sketch is added for her to redraw.
There is no field map. Focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a mechanical technologist owns the fixture drawing before the technician builds it.
research_questions: How often a fixture is modified after the first part is seated?

already_counted.description: Reading the parts drawing, designing the fixture, building it, and seating a part stay bench time.

incremental.description: No template or map to keep. A new fixture is a new job, not weekly upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Design, build and the seat of a part stay with the technician. None of those steps is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lay out cutting lines for machining with drafting tools

steps.what: Read cutting dimensions and datums before machining
Scribe cutting lines on the stock using drafting tools
Check the scribed lines against the drawing before the cut

tasks.design: The technician reads the cutting dimensions in {DOCS}, scribes the lines on the stock with drafting tools, and checks the marks against the drawing. The marked stock then goes to the machinist. No file is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The line is transferred onto metal, and the stock is the artefact.
tasks.enabler_now: A printed layout would still need the technician to mark and check the stock.
tasks.still_hard: The technician still scribes the line and checks it before the cut.
tasks.human_edge: A burr, a bowed edge, or a datum the print does not warn about shows up on the stock.
tasks.altitude: The week is unchanged. The technician still reads the dimensions, scribes the stock, and checks the line.

reach.task: State the finished dimension the layout must hit
reach.learn: Which datum on the drawing is the one the scribe must start from

evidence.claim: Transferring a dimension onto metal with drafting tools is the task. The group's list is drawing paperwork, and no measured drafting result replaces the scribe.

assumptions: Using drafting tools means scribing the stock, not posting a file to a machine.
There is no template to maintain. Focal upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the machinist expects a scribed line or a marked print.
research_questions: How often a scribed line is corrected after the check against the drawing?

already_counted.description: Reading the dimensions, scribing the lines, and checking them before the cut stay bench time.

incremental.description: No layout template to keep. A new drawing is a new job, not weekly upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Reading the dimensions, scribing the stock and checking the line stay manual. None of those steps is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician still builds the prototype, runs the measurement, designs and fits the fixture, and scribes the cut. A numeric re-key does not decide pass or fail.
skills_to_grow: Read an instrument file against a process log, and state the accepted numbers before anything is filed.
Keep alignment, fixture fit, and the scribed line as bench work.
role.ambitious_version: No unattended agent aligns an optic, names a process fault, or marks a cut line.
